answer: Each identity claims one river mooring anchor post, locks an 80-credit bond to it, and files a quill-signed entry in the post log. The first post costs 28; the kth from the same funder costs 28+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6022 and 1000 fakes pay 3,025,000 plus 80,000 locked. An auditor rechecks the log against river traffic: overlapping windows on one post, or one quill key used by two identities, burn the bond. A rented-anchor ring fails: a post cannot be occupied twice at once, and a reused quill key exposes the operator. An honest agent pays 28 and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
